content:
GOAL: Establish the comparison frame for pairwise_1_2 (A=CURVCELL-SID vs B=SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ) on rubric-2026-10-v1.
READ: The prompt's rubric text, both IDEA blocks, and the three evidence bundles (A: e9e97242e0e9ed08; B: 404ea254563870a6; plus the shared cocond bundle bc19762831440f87 which A/B do not use).
OBSERVED: Both finalists draw on identical shared evidence E4-E11 and differ almost entirely in E12/E13 (the proposed geometric operation). All measured numbers in E5-E9 are common to both, so the decision must turn on the proposed rows plus how each idea uses the common measurements.
REASONING: Since the shared bundle cannot separate the candidates, the decisive axes are (a) whether the proposed curvature operation is distinct from the already-measured negatives in E6, (b) whether the off-switches form a matched control, (c) whether the assignment change and observable are named. I will score each idea on those axes rather than on prose quality.
OPEN: Need to check sign/scale consistency of each curvature field and the runnability of each behaviour-off control.

GOAL: Score geometry_necessity and implementability for B (SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ) by checking its own specification for internal consistency.
READ: B spec text ("USE_BEHAVIOUR ... Behaviour off sets all c_p = 1"; "lambda_p(x) = 2/(1 - c_p ||x||^2)") against B evidence E12 ("c_p = -kappa_p in (0.1, 10.0)") and E13 (acts inside quantizer at every level, in assignment score and residual recursion).
OBSERVED: The shipped curvature is defined with a negative sign convention (c_p = -kappa_p, kappa in 0.1..10), but the behaviour-off control sets c_p = +1, i.e. it flips the sign convention rather than holding it fixed and zeroing the behaviour dependence. With latents bounded by tanh (||x|| -> 1) the denominator 1 - c_p||x||^2 goes to 1 - 1*1 = 0 in the control branch, so lambda diverges.
REASONING: A control that changes the sign convention and sits on a pole is not a matched control: it differs from the shipped arm in more than the intended switch. On the rubric this caps falsifiability at 2 ("controls that differ in more than the intended switch") and is a genuine numerical hazard for implementability (B names "deeper levels could become numerically stiff" but specifies no guard/clamp). Also, the shipped operation is a per-node scalar multiply of the residual; a Euclidean control with the same scalar reproduces it, so geometry_necessity is at most 2-3 and the Poincare conformal factor is largely decorative (E12).
OPEN: Whether this alone is decisive, or whether behavioural/downstream evidence also favours A.

GOAL: Score behavior_evidence and downstream_mechanism for both ideas against the shared measured rows.
READ: A hypothesis ("Spearman |A_k| vs B_k clearly positive ... H(next code | level-0 code) will fall ... test Recall@10 above 0.065") vs B hypothesis ("higher per-level code entropy concentrated in the top fanout quartile ... higher training prefix-conditional next-code accuracy"). Shared E5 (successor entropy H 0.931 -> 3.405 across quintiles, support 2.8 -> 44.3, top-1 mass 0.4375 -> 0.0543, Spearman -0.973) and E8 (pair co-membership K=16 0.3106, K=32 0.2164, K=64 0.1547, K=256 0.0822).
OBSERVED: A names the exact assignment change (argmin and commitment at every residual level, per-code cell size s[l][k]) and two observables with an expected direction plus a stated failure statistic (Spearman |A_k| vs B_k ~ 0). B's chain stops at "amplified residuals give hubs more resolution" without saying why multiplying a per-node scalar residual up changes which code is selected at the next level, and its premise (more resolution for high-branching prefixes) runs against E8, where finer first-level capacity is monotonically worse for keeping behavioural neighbours together (0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256).
REASONING: behavior_evidence A ~3-4 (plausible, testable, statistic stated; the B[l][k] cell-level statistic itself is not yet measured, only the item-level E5 analogue), B ~2-3 with a direction that E8 contradicts. downstream_mechanism A ~4 (assignment change + observable + expected direction + diagnostic), B ~2 (hand-waved gap between conformal rescaling and code separation). E5 does support the premise that branching varies hugely, which is the strongest shared asset, and A exploits it at the cell level where the quantizer actually decides.
OPEN: Novelty/exploration comparison against the E6 negative ledger.

GOAL: Score novelty and exploration_value against the measured ledger in E6.
READ: E6 recall@10 for the whole family: l1_br 0.04671, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500, versus l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363. Also E7 per-position NLL for the same runs.
OBSERVED: B's novelty text concedes the prior art is "ranks, transported tangent directions, cones, shells or barycentres" and offers per-node curvature derived from successor fanout. That is a per-node refinement of the same branch-count curvature idea already measured as successor_geodesic_coarse / _v2 (0.05500 / 0.05463) and successor_entropy (0.05122) - four measurements in the same family, all below l1_only 0.06233.
REASONING: B scores novelty ~2 (routine variation of an existing mechanism) and exploration_value ~2 (small variation of a measured mechanism), because its negative result would largely re-confirm an existing negative. A's distinguishing computation is a genuine fixed point: the curvature field is re-estimated from the partition the quantizer is currently producing, so behaviour calibrates curvature, curvature reshapes cells, and reshaped cells re-calibrate behaviour - with curvature entering both argmin and commitment. No row in E6 measures a self-consistent field (successor_entropy is a one-shot static conditioning; geodesic_coarse is global/static curvature; tangent is a transported direction). A scores novelty ~3-4 and exploration_value ~3-4.
OPEN: Consolidate the winner and name its failure risk.

GOAL: Final verdict for pairwise_1_2.
READ: All of the above: A bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08 (E5, E8, E12, E13, spec, hypothesis) and B bundle 404ea254563870a6 (E5, E6, E8, E12, E13, spec switches).
OBSERVED: A is stronger on falsifiability (two genuinely nested off-switches - unit-curvature collapse and curvature removal preserving behaviour weights - plus a stated falsifier in Spearman |A_k| vs B_k and a named discriminating diagnostic), on downstream_mechanism (named assignment change at argmin and commitment, named observable H(next code | level-0 code), named direction and threshold 0.065), on novelty/exploration (self-consistent partition-curvature fixed point is not in the E6 ledger), and on implementability (explicit clamp, no gradient into s, cumulative-mean refresh, 12 scheduled refreshes, quantified +2-4% budget). B is stronger on raw cost (<1%) but that dimension is 10% and A's cost is already negligible.
REASONING: B loses on three counts that are each independently disqualifying at the top of the rubric: its behaviour-off control flips the c_p sign convention of its own E12 (c_p=-kappa_p) to c_p=+1 and therefore sits on the lambda pole; its geometric operation is a per-node scalar residual multiply that a matched Euclidean scalar reproduces; and its premise of finer resolution for hub prefixes is contradicted by E8 (K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822) and sits in the E6 family of four measured negatives. A wins.
FAILURE RISK: A's own listed risk is the live one - the encoder can absorb the field so that Spearman |A_k| vs B_k stays near zero; and the broader family evidence (successor_entropy 0.05122, geodesic_coarse 0.05500) plus E8's coarse-beats-fine result mean the curvature-budget premise may simply be wrong, in which case A lands at or below l1_only 0.06233 rather than above 0.065. Additionally the rescaled distance is not a metric, so cells can empty or become non-convex and the fixed point can drift to a few huge low-curvature cells.
ANSWER: WINNER CURVCELL-SID; FIRST LISTED CURVCELL-SID (A was printed first in the prompt).
